# The Coca-Cola Company Names David Elkins as Incoming Chief Financial Officer


November 23, 2026 4:30 pm EST[Download as PDF](https://investors.coca-colacompany.com/_assets/_a7b2ad45a85aca49778bd55c6eaec90e/cocacolacompany/news/2026-11-23_The_Coca_Cola_Company_Names_David_Elkins_as_1178.pdf)


**Elkins to Succeed John Murphy, Who Will Continue to Serve as President of the Company**


ATLANTA--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- The Coca-Cola Company today announced that David Elkins, a finance leader with extensive experience across global pharmaceuticals and consumer products companies, will become executive vice president and chief financial officer of Coca-Cola April 2, 2027, succeeding John Murphy.


David Elkins, incoming EVP and CFO at The Coca-Cola Company


Elkins has served as EVP and CFO of Bristol Myers Squibb since 2019, and his past roles include positions with Johnson & Johnson and AstraZeneca.


Murphy, 64, intends to retire in 2027, with timing determined later to allow for a smooth and orderly leadership transition for the CFO role. Murphy, who has been CFO since 2019, has been working with company leadership for some time to prepare for the succession process.


Murphy will continue to serve as president, focusing on key enterprise priorities in 2027, in addition to the CFO transition. As CFO, Elkins’ oversight will include finance, global strategy and Enterprise Services.


Elkins and Murphy will both report to CEO Henrique Braun.


“John has been a transformational leader during his 38 years at Coca-Cola, especially through his most recent service as president and CFO,” Braun said. “I am very happy John will ensure a smooth transition and provide valuable perspective as we maintain our focus on growing the company.”


“David comes to Coca-Cola with a track record of success across complex, global companies,” Braun said. “He brings a strong understanding of finance and has developed future leaders. He will bring complementary skills to our highly experienced leadership team.”


**More About David Elkins**


Elkins, 58, has been responsible for the Global Business Operations organization at Bristol Myers Squibb, which consists of finance, business development, Global Financial Services & Operational Excellence, procurement and investor relations.


Elkins joined the company in 2019 when it acquired Celgene, where he was serving as EVP and CFO. He joined Celgene in 2018 after several years at Johnson & Johnson, where he was CFO for the consumer products and medical device businesses and corporate functions.


Earlier, Elkins held roles with Becton, Dickinson, a leading global medical device company, and pharmaceutical and biotechnology company AstraZeneca. He began his career in finance at The Boeing Co.


Elkins is a member of the board of directors of Tapestry Inc.


Elkins earned a bachelor’s degree in economics from the University of Delaware, a master’s degree in organizational dynamics from the University of Pennsylvania and an MBA from Drexel University.


**About John Murphy**


Murphy was named CFO in 2019 and president in 2022. From 2016 to 2018, he served as president of the company’s Asia Pacific group.


Murphy began his career with Coca-Cola in 1988 and went on to hold a variety of general management, finance and strategic planning roles around the world.


For more about Murphy’s background, visit[https://www.coca-colacompany.com/about-us/leadership/john-murphy](https://www.coca-colacompany.com/about-us/leadership/john-murphy)


**About The Coca-Cola Company**


The Coca-Cola Company (NYSE: KO) is a total beverage company with products sold in more than 200 countries and territories. Our company’s purpose is to refresh the world and make a difference. We sell multiple billion-dollar brands across several beverage categories worldwide. Our portfolio of sparkling soft drink brands includes Coca-Cola, Sprite and Fanta. Our water, sports, coffee and tea brands include Dasani, smartwater, vitaminwater, Topo Chico, BODYARMOR, Powerade, Costa, Georgia, Fuze Tea, Gold Peak and Ayataka. Our juice, value-added dairy and plant-based beverage brands include Minute Maid, Simply, innocent, Del Valle, fairlife and Santa Clara. We’re constantly transforming our portfolio, from reducing sugar in our drinks to bringing innovative new products to market. We seek to positively impact people’s lives, communities and the planet through water replenishment, packaging recycling, sustainable sourcing practices and carbon emissions reductions across our value chain. Together with our bottling partners, we employ more than 700,000 people, helping bring economic opportunity to local communities worldwide.
